Load mixture (consumer) data

Source: R/load.R
load_mix_data.Rd

Reads the consumer data file and records the model's random, fixed and continuous effects, exactly as MixSIAR::load_mix_data() does, with the same arguments.

Usage

load_mix_data(
  filename,
  iso_names,
  factors,
  fac_random,
  fac_nested,
  cont_effects
)

Arguments

filename

Path of the consumer .csv file (or a data frame with its contents): one row per consumer, one column per tracer and per effect.

iso_names

Names of the tracer columns to use, e.g. c("d13C", "d15N").

factors

Names of the categorical effect columns (0, 1 or 2), or NULL.

fac_random

Logical, one per factor: TRUE for a random effect, FALSE for a fixed effect.

fac_nested

Logical, one per factor: TRUE for a factor nested within the other (only with two random effects), or NULL.

cont_effects

Name of a continuous effect column (0 or 1), or NULL.

Value

A list with MixSIAR's fields (data, data_iso, n.iso, n.re, n.fe, n.ce, n.effects, FAC, CE, CE_orig, CE_center, CE_scale, cont_effects, MU_names, SIG_names, iso_names, N, factors, fac_random, fac_nested, fere). As in MixSIAR, a fixed effect is put before a random one.

Examples

mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "wolves_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = c("Region", "Pack"),
  fac_random = c(TRUE, TRUE), fac_nested = c(FALSE, TRUE), cont_effects = NULL)
